articles.title: What FSU head coach Mike Norvell said after losing to Miami
articles.summary: The Miami Hurricanes beat the FSU Seminoles in double overtime. Here is what Mike Norvell had to say after the game.
articles.body:
The FSU Seminoles and Miami Hurricanes played another classic game, with the Seminoles falling 43-35 in double overtime. Unfortunately, there was plenty of controversy surrounding the final two plays of the game as FSU tried to tie the game.

Xavier Chaplin was called for a holding call, wiping out a touchdown throw from Ashton Daniels to Micahi Danzy on 4th and 21. Daniels then appeared to throw a touchdown to Duce Robinson on 4th and 31, but the officials ruled it an interception, ending the game. Head coach Mike Norvell revealed after the game that he did not get an explanation for the final play, voicing his frustration with the situation.

"I didn't get an explanation," he said. " They went to review. It's pretty unique when you have the same crew. Back-to-back years, game-ending situations that go down on the last play. You don't get a whole lot of explanation. You had a holding call on the play before. I watched the replay.

"Since the start of football, if it's a tie, it goes to the receiver. I guess they had a different angle. You could see something different. I'm sure that they will evaluate that and see."

He also voiced his frustrations with the play before, indicating he did not agree with the holding call on Chaplin.

"Holding call on the play before," Norvell said. "They said it was on 77. Go watch the film.

"It's unfortunate to see the guys go out there and perform the way they did. Like I said, there's plenty of plays. To have that outcome come down to a play like that. I'm grateful for our guys and the way they battled."

Norvell also talked about how proud he is of the team, potentially going for two in overtime, and more. Here are his comments after FSU's controversial loss.

First off, just a disappointing result in the game that I'm really proud of our players. The way they came out, the way they battled, obviously competing at a high level throughout. I had high expectations of what it would look like, what it would be.

Seeing the way that they went back and forth, there's plays in all phases that you like to have back. We had opportunities, but those guys competed to the very end. For the ending to be like that, just sick.

I am proud of our players. We've got to continue to push, got to continue to improve. They're hurting, we're hurting, and everybody in that game, it means so much. To see the way that they fought through it.

We had missed opportunities. There's times that obviously we've got to be a lot better, but I thought our guys battled. I think that's what this rivalry is about. I asked if we could show the heart and show the type of men they are. I thought that they all did. Players, coaches, the work that went in. They continued to fight in belief.

Just as I told them thereafter, that's not stopping. This team is going to continue to pour everything they have into it. Results are not what we want.

Results are, we lost to some good football teams. We played really good football. at times we've got to be more consistent in that.

I'm grateful for these guys in the locker room and the work that they poured in, put themselves in the position that they did tonight.

On the explanation he got on the final play from the refs

They went to review. It's pretty unique when you have the same crew. Back-to-back years, game-ending situations that go down on the last play. You don't get a whole lot of explanation. You had a holding call on the play before. I watched the replay.

Since the start of football, if it's a tie, it goes to the receiver. I guess they had a different angle. You could see something different. I'm sure that they will evaluate that and see.

Holding call on the play before. They said it was on 77. Go watch the film.

It's unfortunate to see the guys go out there and perform the way they did. Like I said, there's plenty of plays. To have that outcome come down to a play like that. I'm grateful for our guys and the way they battled.

On if he considered going for two in the first overtime

It did cross my mind. There in the moment. With just a little bit of the time there. That's probably what kept me from it, but it was a consideration. I was really proud of the way our guys went out there.

Obviously, Duce, we talked throughout the course of this week; he's just somebody who cares so much. I told him, When you go into the game, you control everything you can control.

There will be times when the ball comes to you. I think you had a good number of targets tonight. There will be times when it doesn't.

You just focus on doing your job. Being ready for it. For him to make the three plays that he made at the end. The last play was a hell of a play that he made. It didn't go in our way. For him to do that, it was really special.

Seeing the way he competed. The way he was able to perform there. Obviously, AD made some big throws there at the end. Hurt for this team.

On if this game coming down to the wire affects his decisions on fourth down

We had the fourth downs near the goal line.

This game, you never know how things are going to unfold. I was playing a very explosive football team. Number one offense, number one defense in the country. You've got to play to win. Our defense did a great job. We got stopped. Gave us a short field. Ended up being able to convert, get points on the board.

We want to score every time we have a football. Those are tough decisions. Unfortunately, we haven't been good enough in them these last two weeks. You evaluate all things situationally within a game. Who? What? All things you do in your planning.

That was the reason for the decision. That was probably the reason they went for it. On their two fourth downs, they didn't get.

To be honest, I don't have the update. I just love the kid. To see somebody that's hurting the way he was hurting. He's such a competitor. He's tough.

Like I said, I don't know the final deal with the foot injury. Even with that, he's hopping to get across. When I went out there, I just told him 'Look at me everything's going to be okay. Whatever it is. It will all be good.' I just wanted him to calm down. Just to see his teammates, them surrounding him.

We got a great group of young men. I'm honored to see them play for each other. The things that they pour in. The challenges that they embrace. We try to push in all areas. For what they're doing on the field. What they're doing off the field. Who they're getting to do it with. To feel those guys come together. We were hurting for Ous. Obviously, the next guy's got to be ready. Everybody's got to take it up another notch when your top playmaker goes down, I thought they did that.

On the final two plays by Ashton Daniels

You saw it. Obviously, AD made the throw on both of them. He made the throw on both of them. But you saw the competitiveness of the receivers.

For Machi, it was a rough game for him a little early. He didn't have a whole lot of opportunities. But you saw a determination to go up and make that play. I was really proud of him. And how he was able to stay in it.

For Ashlynd to give him an opportunity. The 7 cut to Duce for the touchdown. For the play to Machi. The throw there at the end, having to extend for Duce's catch, the last play deal.

That was impressive. To see those guys compete. It's unfortunate that it didn't finish the way we wanted it to finish. We've got to learn from it. We've got to grow from it. We've got to get better and be more consistent.

Because there's plays throughout from first quarter to fourth quarter. And in overtime. That we have to make. That we've got to be able to beat a top team.

Which I said, I believe in the capabilities of this team. I think they showed that they have that. It's just the consistency. We've got to continue to grow. There are plays that cost us throughout that we've got to get cleaned up.

On what he said to Duce after that play, the team

I told them it hurts. The result hurts. My respect for them, because going into this week. I told them I want to see their heart, I want to see their fight, I want to see their passion, I want to see the love they have for each other, the love for playing this game. I want to see the type of men they were. Same thing for the coaches.

I thought the coaches and staff did a really good job putting together a game plan. Where you play a team that's one in both categories, it's a talented team. They've invested what they can do to have a really talented team.

We came in here with absolutely no other focus other then to go win. I believe we can do that. We have a team that is very capable. I hurt for them.

But I also told them how proud of them I am. Because I am proud of them.

We're not looking to play a close type of game. We want the results. But how that ended. That's what pisses me off. Because they went and made some plays in those moments. And you know. It is what it is.

On what it takes to come through in those crucial moments to steal a game

It wouldn't have been stealing one. We went and played our butts off in that game. We didn't make the plays necessary. It was two competitive teams that went through it.

And obviously they made the plays that were necessary offensively there in overtime. We had opportunities, but we were not able to capitalize.

All the emotion, everything that's going around you still make it small. Technique. Fundamentals. Communication.

I give credit to them, made a hell of a throw and catch to Toney there. Jabril's in a really good place, and they pretty much had to be dang near perfect on it. Had the big run, we had a mistake that showed up there.

Those are the things, you've got to eliminate that. And I mean, just like on their end I'm sure they're sitting there talking about some of the mistakes they had. It happens in a game of football. At the end of the day. You've got to make those critical plays. It was a critical play in the second quarter. It was a critical play in the third quarter, fourth quarter, all parts of it.

You remember for how they finished, I'd have liked to have seen just a couple more plays because I thought those guys were competeting to do whatever they need to do. But unfortunately the outcome is the outcome.

articles.title: Will 49ers WR Mike Evans play on Monday vs Commanders?
articles.summary: Will 49ers star wide receiver Mike Evans play against the Commanders on Monday Night Football?
articles.body:
Will future Hall of Fame wide receiver Mike Evans play for the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night against the Washington Commanders ?

The 13-year veteran, in his first year for the 49ers after 12 incredible seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , has been outstanding through San Francisco's first five games. Evans has caught 24 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns and has looked like he hasn't missed a beat in a new offense.

However, Evans has battled a rib injury since Week 3. Last week, Evans added another injury, a sore Achilles, according to head coach Kyle Shanahan.

He did not practice all week. With the game on Monday, injured players got an extra day of rest, but Evans still didn't practice on Saturday. He did conditioning work on the side. Shanahan listed Evans as questionable for Monday's game against the Commanders.

"We'll know on Monday, I think," Shanahan said of Evans.

Considering Evans' veteran status, it would be a surprise if he didn't suit up against Washington. He missed some practice time earlier this season but hasn't missed a game.

While Evans' status is questionable until Monday's game, the 49ers' offense could get some important veterans back. 10-time Pro Bowl fullback Kyle Juszczyk is expected to return on Monday after missing last week's game with a knee sprain and bone bruise.

The 49ers could also get wide receiver Christian Kirk back for Monday night. The nine-year veteran signed a one-year deal with the 49ers in the offseason, and he has yet to make his San Francisco debut. Kirk has been out with a calf injury since the start of training camp. Shanahan said Kirk could be activated in time for Monday night's game.

articles.title: Kim Little and Frida Maanum updates after Birmingham draw
articles.summary: Kim Little and Frida Maanum were both missing as Arsenal were held by Birmingham City, with the club confirming separate medical reasons for their absences.P...
articles.body:
Kim Little and Frida Maanum were both missing as Arsenal were held by Birmingham City, with the club confirming separate medical reasons for their absences.

Kim Little missed Arsenal 's 1-1 draw with Birmingham City on Saturday because of illness, while Frida Maanum was ruled out with a muscle injury.

Little's absence was attributed simply to illness. Arsenal did not specify the nature of it , when it began or how long she might be unavailable, and no return date was given.

Her absence, combined with the injury to Mariona Caldentey that will see her out for up to 10 weeks, forced changes in midfield.

Alessia Russo was used alongside Georgia Stanway and Kyra Cooney-Cross , while Leah Williamson captained the side in Little's absence.

Maanum's situation was similarly limited in detail. Arsenal's update said: "Frida Maanum misses out on the matchday squad with a muscle injury."

The club did not identify which muscle was affected, how serious the injury was, when it happened or how long she might be out.

The absences left Renee Slegers without Little and Maanum as well as Caldentey and Selina Cerci , who has undergone knee surgery.

That reduced Arsenal's midfield and attacking options and contributed to the reshuffle that saw Russo move deeper, Stina Blackstenius start up front and Olivia Smith return to the starting XI.

Smith's superb second-half goal rescued a point for Arsenal, but after six games, the team is languishing on just six points. They are in eight place at the time of writing, with five of the six teams below them still to play this weekend. Brighton could leapfrog the Gunners but they are away to Manchester City on Sunday afternoon. Crystal Palace , however, could go above Arsenal with a home win over West Ham .

articles.body:
SC Freiburg's Philipp Treu has revealed that Joshua Kimmich of Bayern Munich impressed him the most in the Germany national team.

"As a kid and teenager, I always looked up to him as an inspiration," the 25-year-old said during an interview with BILD.

"It was impressive to get to know him as a person, but also to watch him on the pitch. It starts right from the warm-up.

"He's already sweating while riding the bike and always gives 100 percent. You always hear about how extremely ambitious he is.

"You hear how badly he wants to win – but experiencing that for myself was really cool. I can also take that mentality into my own life.

"He wants to win every game and always get the very best out of himself. That makes him a role model for many," explained Treu.

Now doubt these will come as words of slight comfort for Kimmich, who recently has been called into question regarding his role for Germany .

articles.title: Cathy Engelbert issues a warning to next WNBA Commissioner in her last press conference
articles.summary: With Cathy Engelbert stepping down as WNBA Commissioner, she has some advice for her successor that they may want to keep in mind. The WNBA has grown exponen...
articles.body:
With Cathy Engelbert stepping down as WNBA Commissioner, she has some advice for her successor that they may want to keep in mind.

The WNBA has grown exponentially since 2024, the league is currently going through an incredible period of transition. More people are watching than ever before, the numbers continue to grow at a rapid rate, and the future is even brighter with young superstars like Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese, and Paige Bueckers.

But more eyeballs bring more scrutiny, nothing is ever that simple. No one knows that better than WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert. During her seven years in charge, and especially the last couple, she has been tasked with challenge after challenge. She has failed sometimes in the eyes of a few, but her experience and insight into the process is second to none.

Cathy Engelbert warns next commissioner they need to have a 'thick skin' and a lot of confidence

2026 has been a volatile year for the W. Even as they reach unprecedented heights, the league's hierarchy has had to deal with working out a new CBA (Collective Bargaining Agreement) and handle the highly controversial debate surrounding trans athletes.

Engelbert has been at the receiving end of hate from lots of fans and analysts alike, which may inform some of the advice she is passing on to her successor.

"The good news is there's people who really want to take on this role, which I think is great. It's a multidimensional role. You have to have very thick skin," Engelbert said during her final press conference as the top boss of the WNBA.

"You have to have confidence that we can continue this growth trajectory and confidence in building relationships with players and agents and the Board of Governors, the owners and the stakeholders."

It is an exciting opportunity for the person that takes up the role. But in such a delicate period when it comes to growth and transition, they will need to have conviction, vision, and fortitude to keep it going. Engelbert's words will come in handy whenever they arrive at the next big crossroads moment for the league.

articles.title: Where do the Lions rank in the NFC right now?
articles.summary: Where do the Detroit Lions rank in the NFC after five weeks of the 2026 season?
articles.body:
The NFC isn't looking quite as strong as it did even a few weeks ago.

This week kicked off with the Seattle Seahawks losing their third game of the season. Last year, the Super Bowl champions lost just three total games for the entire 2025 season. What was thought to be clearly the best division in football—the NFC West—now just has a single team with a winning record. The 49ers are 5-0, the Seahawks are 3-3, the Los Angeles Rams are 2-3, and the Arizona Cardinals are just 1-4.

Beyond that division, the NFC East is looking like a mess. The New York Giants and their very unconvincing 3-1-1 record lead the division, while everyone else is below .500. Personally, I had a belief that the Philadelphia Eagles would pull themselves out of their 2-3 hole, but with the news that quarterback Jalen Hurts is now on injured reserve indefinitely with a blood clot issue, I'm not sure Tanner McKee and his two career starts is ready to turn things around.

Elsewhere, it doesn't look like the Saints are as good as the Lions made them look in Week 2, but the Atlanta Falcons are on the rise. And, of course, the NFC North is pretty strong top to bottom.

Where do the Lions rank in the NFC right now?

My answer: Officially, the Lions are in the seventh spot in the NFC, when it comes to playoff standings. The 49ers, Vikings, Giants, and Panthers all lead their divisions. While the three Wild Card teams are the Packers, Bears, and Lions, in that order.

As to how I feel the Lions rank, there are two teams that are easily ahead of the Lions: the undefeated 49ers and Vikings. Say what you will about the Vikings' resume or their offensive struggles, that defense is raising hell right now, and it's seriously impressive. I don't think I need to make a case for San Francisco.

Personally, I still think the Rams are better than the Lions, and it will show in their next five games when Los Angeles plays the Cardinals, Raiders, Chargers, Commanders, and Cardinals. Nothing is guaranteed in the NFL, but that feels like five straight wins.

We also have to talk about the Carolina Panthers. They may have a worse record (2-2) than the Lions (3-2), but they beat them straight up and fairly decisively. Objectively, you have to give them the edge.

A couple of weeks ago, I ranked the Lions' third in the NFC North behind the Vikings and Bears , and I don't think my opinion of the division has changed despite Green Bay's statement win over Chicago last week.

So that puts the 49ers, Vikings, Bears, Rams, and Panthers all ahead of Detroit.

I think the Seahawks, Packers, and Falcons are all right there on the same tier with the Lions, and that's it. So I'd have the Lions anywhere from sixth to ninth in the NFC. For now, I'll put them at seventh because I still believe Seattle will turn things around despite some serious struggles on offense and a step back on defense.

articles.title: Jets' David Bailey is making a sacrifice to accelerate his development
articles.summary: The Jets' star rookie pass rusher David Bailey is accelerate his development by making this decision.
articles.body:
The New York Jets have plenty of reasons to be excited about David Bailey and his development after his dominant performance against the Cleveland Browns . The young edge rusher recorded three sacks and four additional quarterback hits on Deshaun Watson, helping lead a defensive effort that produced eight sacks in a 17-12 victory .

Now, fans are learning more about the habits behind Bailey's growing success, including one decision that removes a familiar distraction from his daily routine. David Bailey is choosing development over distraction. He recently revealed how he's sharpening his focus.

Bailey deleted his social media apps after Week 1, explaining that he wanted to spend less time scrolling and more time on activities that could benefit his football career. Speaking with reporters recently , he detailed why he made the change.

"I felt like I was spending too much time. Time I could've spent on other things...putting more time into my body, studying the playbook. Other productive things I could've been doing," Bailey said.

The decision offers an interesting glimpse into how Bailey approaches his development. Rather than getting caught up in the attention surrounding his performances, he is prioritizing the work that happens away from the field. Bailey's breakout against Cleveland has raised expectations, but one outstanding afternoon is only the beginning of the conversation.

If he continues refining his technique, studying opposing offenses and investing in his physical development, the Jets could have an increasingly disruptive force leading their pass rush. The question now is how high Bailey's ceiling might be. His latest performance has certainly given Jets fans another reason to keep watching.

articles.title: Iowa women's wrestling's Kylie Welker wins U23 World title
articles.summary: Iowa women's wrestling's Kylie Welker wins U23 World Championship
articles.body:
Iowa women's wrestling's Kylie Welker left Las Vegas a big winner, securing her third consecutive U23 World Championship on Oct. 17.

The Hawkeye senior and national champion steamrolled her way through competition at 76 kilograms for Team USA. Welker outscored opponents 38-0 and had three technical falls and a pin.

Welker began her run with a 11-0 technical fall win over Poland's Patrycja Cube, recording four takedowns in the win. A win by fall over Turkey's Elmira Yasin sent her to the semifinals, where Welker earned her second 11-0 technical fall of the tournament over Russia's Mariia Silina to make the finals. She capped off her stellar outing with a 10-0 technical fall over Serbia's Evelin Ujhelji in the finals with one takedown and four leg laces, winning in just 47 seconds.

Welker is the first American to win three U23 World titles and the first women's freestyle wrestler to do so in consecutive years according to USA Wrestling. Welker is now a four-time age-group World champion with a U20 World title under her belt as she readies for her final collegiate season.

"It feels pretty special," Welker told USA Wrestling. "It's always my goal to go out there and do the best I can. World gold is what I strive for, so it feels good."

Also winning hardware for Iowa women's wrestling and Team USA at the U23 World Championships was Everest Leydecker (55 kilograms) and Reese Larramendy (65 kilograms). Both walked away with U23 World bronze medals.

Leydecker opened with three consecutive technical falls to reach the semifinals. She led 3-0 in the semifinal bout but Hungary's Gerda Terek caught Leydecker in a cradle and won by fall to secure an upset win. Leydecker returned in dominant fashion and defeated Uzbekistan's Ulmeken Esenbaeva by an 11-0 technical fall, with two takedowns and three leg laces to secure her bronze medal.

Larramendy began her tournament with a 6-4 win by decision over Colombia's Nicoll Parrado Osorio, showing some nice counter-offense in the first period and holding on from there to win. She fell in a quick 10-0 technical fall in the semifinals to China's Yuqi Rao. Larramendy returned and won a 10-4 decision over Ayse Erkan of Turkey to secure U23 World bronze.

This was Larramendy's first medal at the World level. Leydecker, a two-time U20 World champion, added more to her trophy case with her efforts and isn't done yet as she has a spot at the Senior World Championships from Oct. 24-Nov. 1. Both will be national-title contenders for Iowa women's wrestling this season.

Also representing the Hawkeyes and Team USA at the U23 World Championships was men's wrestler Jordan Williams at 70 kilograms in freestyle. He opened with back-to-back wins by decision, starting with defeating Spain's Kodakov Gil in a one takedown bout ending in a 3-1 decision. Against India's Sumit Bharaskar, a takedown and exposure in the first period carried Williams to a 6-4 victory by decision.

In the quarterfinals, he faced Moldova's Alexandr Gaidarli, a multiple-time age-group medalist. Williams suffered a 10-0 technical fall loss and since Gaidarli did not reach the finals, Williams was not pulled back into the repechage to compete for bronze. He'll compete for a starting spot in the middleweights for the Hawkeyes this upcoming season.

Iowa State Cyclones men's heavyweight Coby Merrill rounded out the field for Iowans at the U23 World Championships at 125 kilograms for Team USA. He began with a 11-0 technical fall over Armenia's Khachatryan Khachatur, showcasing a variety of offense in the bout. His next bout ended in a loss to Georgia's Aleksandre Abramishvili in a quick 10-0 technical fall, highlighted by several double-leg takedowns.

Merrill was pulled back into the repechage and made the bronze-medal match after a 10-0 technical fall win over Canada's Mahil Karanveer Singh. With hardware on the line, Merrill cruised past Hungary's Gellen Milan. He had one takedown into two gut wrenches, followed by four step-outs for a 10-0 technical fall and bronze medal. The Cyclone freshman projects to start at heavyweight this year for Iowa State.

Eli McKown covers high school sports and wrestling for the Des Moines Register. Contact him at Emckown@gannett.com . Follow him on Twitter at @EMcKown23.

articles.title: Buy or Sell the Latest NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Nearly three weeks into the 2026-27 NHL regular season, trade rumors are swirling around several notable stars.
articles.body:
Nearly three weeks into the 2026-27 NHL regular season, trade rumors are swirling around several notable stars.

A season-ending injury to New York Rangers starting goaltender Igor Shesterkin sparked speculation about whether they might pursue Winnipeg Jets holdout Connor Hellebuyck.

Meanwhile, Montréal Canadiens fans serenaded Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin with chants of "We want Larkin" during a recent game between the two clubs at the Bell Centre. That prompted some observers to wonder if it could lead to Larkin agreeing to a trade to Montréal.

How much stock should we put in that conjecture? Follow along as we examine the five most notable trade rumors to determine which ones are worth buying or selling.

On Oct. 10, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the Vancouver Canucks were among the teams interested in Connor Zary. Earlier that week, the Calgary Flames waived and demoted the 25-year-old forward to their AHL affiliate.

The Flames chose Zary in the first round of the 2020 NHL Draft. A versatile forward who can play center or wing, he had a promising NHL debut in 2023-24, scoring 14 goals and 20 assists for 34 points in 63 games.

However, injuries hampered Zary's development over the next two seasons. He's signed through 2027-28 with an average annual value of $3.8 million. According to Friedman, a trade to the Canucks didn't seem imminent.

Canucks beat writer Thomas Drance of The Athletic likes Zary's game but noted his lack of size and physicality, singling out his below-average skating. Nevertheless, he thinks Zary could be a good reclamation project if another asset were included, or if the Flames would take back a contract the Canucks wanted to move.

The Canucks could be interested in Zary, but it doesn't seem like they (or other clubs) are currently keen to acquire him. That could change if he rebuilds his game in the AHL or if he performs well whenever the Flames recall him.

Alexander Nikishin Could Return to the Carolina Hurricanes

A fixture in the rumor mill since June, defenseman Alexander Nikishin sat at No. 3 on our October NHL Trade Block Big Board . He reportedly requested a trade soon after the Carolina Hurricanes won the Stanley Cup in June.

Since then, there's no indication the Hurricanes will be moving him anytime soon. A rumored deal with the New York Rangers fell through . The 25-year-old defenseman was linked to the St. Louis Blues and Nashville Predators, but there is no indication that any serious trade discussions took place.

Nikishin is coming off his entry-level contract. He's a restricted free agent, but his limited number of NHL games makes him ineligible to sign an offer sheet.

On Oct. 10, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman suggested the possibility of Nikishin returning to Carolina. He doesn't see any trade possibilities on the horizon, speculating that the Hurricanes would bring him back this season if the two sides can agree to a new contract.

Nikishin's rumored asking price of a five-year deal worth $9 million annually makes him difficult to move. So has the uncertainty over whether he'd agree to sign with clubs interested in acquiring him. He might have to accept a one-year deal that would be worth less than his asking price to return to the Hurricanes.

Philadelphia Flyers Could Make a Big Trade

After reaching the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Philadelphia Flyers lurched from the gate this season with a 0-6-3 record in their first nine games. Some of their fans recently booed the team off the ice, while others called for head coach Rick Tocchet to be fired .

Multiple pundits, including Flyers beat writer Kevin Kurz of The Athletic and Daily Faceoff's Anthony Di Marco, reported that Tocchet's job is safe for now. They also wondered if a trade might right the ship and which players could become trade bait.

Kurz noted the Flyers have several young players under long- and short-term contracts who lack any sort of no-trade protection. They include Trevor Zegras, Jamie Drysdale, Noah Cates, Tyson Foerster, Matvei Michkov, and Cam York.

Di Marco suggested long-time Flyers such as Cates, Owen Tippett, and Travis Konecny as potential trade chips. He cited team sources claiming Konency's style of play was becoming a source of frustration and suggested he could be asked to waive his no-movement clause if things didn't improve.

On Oct. 13, TSN's Pierre LeBrun reported that Flyers general manager Daniel Briere was getting plenty of calls, but no offers that would provide immediate help. LeBrun believes there's no blockbuster trade or easy fix to get the Flyers out of this mess, suggesting they'll have to deal with this internally.

Connor Hellebuyck to the New York Rangers

A season-ending leg injury suffered by superstar goaltender Igor Shesterkin threatens to derail the New York Rangers' strong start. Some pundits wonder if it would force general manager Chris Drury to make a pitch for Connor Hellebuyck of the Winnipeg Jets.

A three-time Vezina Trophy winner, Hellebuyck went public with his trade request in August. The 33-year-old goaltender didn't report to training camp last month and remains suspended by the Jets without pay as he sits at home in Michigan awaiting a trade.

ESPN's Kevin Weekes included Hellebuyck among his list of suggested trade and free-agent options for the Rangers. Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman found the idea intriguing , calling it a move he'd love to see.

However, Friedman doesn't expect it to happen. The Score's Josh Wegman shared that opinion . Adam Gretz considered it "not logical," noting that Hellebuyck and Shesterkin would cost a combined $20 million in salary-cap space. TSN's Darren Dreger said the two teams spoke , but the Rangers won't pay the asking price.

For now, the Rangers are sticking with backup Dylan Garand and call-up Spencer Martin. They'll also get Joonas Korpisalo back from injured reserve next month. We can't rule out the possibility of them shopping for an experienced starter, but it won't be Hellebuyck.

It's no secret the Montréal Canadiens are in the market for a top-six forward. They reportedly came close to acquiring Matthew Knies from the Toronto Maple Leafs at the March trade deadline. The Habs also pursued Kirill Marchenko before the Columbus Blue Jackets sent him to Toronto for Knies.

The Canadiens would prefer a reliable second-line center, but such talent is currently scarce in the trade market. Dylan Larkin of the Detroit Red Wings is the only one available after requesting a trade this summer, but his list of preferred trade destinations excludes the seven Canadian teams.

Nevertheless, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Oct.8 that people were trying to talk Larkin into joining the rising young Canadiens team. He believes he'd be a perfect fit as their second-line center behind team captain and Selke Trophy winner Nick Suzuki.

Canadiens fans, spurred by Montréal radio host Georges Laraque, chanted "We want Larkin" during the Red Wings-Canadiens game in Montreal on Oct. 10. Larkin heard the chants and appreciated them, but it doesn't appear that they convinced him to accept a trade to Montréal.

Larkin would be a terrific candidate to address the Canadiens' need for a second-line center. However, he has full control over his situation, and that doesn't include coming to Montreal, no matter how loudly Canadiens fans chant his name.

articles.title: Winners and losers from FSU's thriller vs Miami
articles.summary: Florida State pushed Miami to double overtime despite entering as a heavy underdog, but the Seminoles fell 43-35 after a controversial final sequence.
articles.body:
Florida State left Hard Rock Stadium with another loss Saturday night, but this one looked nothing like the result many expected entering rivalry week. The Seminoles entered as roughly three-touchdown underdogs against No. 3 Miami, with Mike Norvell's job security already under intense scrutiny following a 44-20 loss at Louisville.

Instead of another lopsided defeat, FSU traded punches with an unbeaten Hurricanes team, led 21-14 in the second half and eventually forced double overtime before falling 43-35. The ending only added to the frustration .

There are no moral victories for a program now sitting at 3-4, but there were still meaningful positives, and some familiar problems in FSU's latest rivalry loss. Here are the winners and losers from FSU's heartbreaking loss to Miami.

Winner: Ashton Daniels answers the moment

Daniels delivered arguably his most impressive performance as a Seminole considering the opponent and circumstances. The quarterback completed 15 of 28 passes for 298 yards and four touchdowns, while adding 31 rushing yards and another score.

His biggest play came with FSU trailing 28-21 late in the fourth quarter, when he connected with Duce Robinson for a 75-yard touchdown after Miami retook the lead. Daniels then found Robinson again for a 20-yard score in the first overtime. The interception on the final Hail Mary will go on his stat line, but it hardly tells the story of his night.

Loser: Florida State's run defense remains a major concern

The effort improved from Louisville, but the underlying problem did not disappear. Miami rushed for 257 yards on 44 attempts, averaging 5.8 yards per carry. Javian Mallory led the Hurricanes with 108 yards and two touchdowns on 13 attempts, including a 25-yard touchdown in overtime.

FSU surrendered 583 total yards overall, making it difficult for the defense to consistently get off the field despite producing several important stops.

Florida State had already overcome enough to give itself one final chance. Then came a brutal finish.

Daniels appeared to connect with Danzy for a touchdown on fourth-and-21, only for holding on Xavier Chaplin to wipe the play away. Facing fourth-and-31, Daniels threw into the end zone again, where Fitzgerald was awarded the interception after a contested battle for the football. The replay official reviewed the play and allowed the call to stand.

Whether Florida State fans agree with the ruling or not , the ending will sting because the Seminoles had somehow given themselves an opportunity to tie the game after entering the night as massive underdogs.

Winner: Duce Robinson delivers his breakout moment

Robinson gave Florida State the explosive receiving performance it desperately needed. The future NFL wide receiver finished with five catches for 113 yards and two touchdowns, including the 75-yard fourth-quarter score that immediately tied the game and the touchdown that put FSU ahead in the first overtime.

Against one of the biggest opponents on the schedule, Robinson looked every bit like the matchup problem Florida State expected him to become.

Winner: FSU's response under Mike Norvell

A loss still leaves Norvell facing difficult questions. Florida State is below .500 through seven games, and Saturday does not erase the problems that created pressure around the program.

However, after collapsing at Louisville, the Seminoles went on the road as 21.5-point underdogs and pushed the No. 3 team in the country into a second overtime. FSU trailed twice in the fourth quarter and overtime and answered both times.

That does not solve Norvell's long-term situation, but it was a considerably different performance from the type of embarrassing defeat many feared could intensify his immediate hot-seat pressure.

The most concerning development of the night may have come before halftime. Kromah was carted off after suffering a left leg injury late in the second quarter. An air cast was placed on his leg before he was taken to the locker room. He had 44 yards on 14 carries before leaving the game.

His status becomes one of the biggest things to monitor coming out of rivalry weekend.
